It uses deterministic mock data and is not intended for production use. Selecting it REPLACES the template's own calculator / current_utc_time; no gateway, IAM grant, or extra dependency is required.
configure.agentSdkNote: The Claude Agent SDK brings its own agentic loop — subagents via .claude/agents, hooks and MCP servers — and reads models from Bedrock (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1). It is the only SDK in this category today.

configure.kbEmpty: no active knowledge bases · create one first
configure.kbNote: Harness agents get the knowledge bases attached as gateway retrieval tools (per-KB search plus multi-step agentic retrieval). The description you gave each KB guides when the agent queries it.
configure.kbNoteDirect: The generated agent gets two tools that query these knowledge bases through the Bedrock retrieval API with its execution role: kb_search (one similarity search, fast) and kb_deep_search (agentic multi-step — plans sub-queries and returns a cited answer, slower and more expensive). Changing the selection needs a re-publish.
configure.a2aNote: A2A agents serve the standard Agent-to-Agent protocol (JSON-RPC on the runtime endpoint, agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json). The Registry card advertises the real endpoint and the skills below — other agents route by them. Chat works as usual; config-bundle experiments don't apply.

how.title: HOW ONLINE EVALUATION WORKS
how.s1: SAMPLE — a share (sampling %) of live sessions is picked from the agent's runtime log group, optionally narrowed by filters
how.s2: WAIT — a session counts as complete once it has been idle for the session timeout
how.s3: JUDGE — each evaluator scores the session; results land in the results log group and as CloudWatch metrics (Bedrock-AgentCore/Evaluations)
how.s4: READ — this page aggregates the results log group with Logs Insights; the metrics can drive CloudWatch alarms
how.s5: COST — judge invocations = sampled sessions × evaluators; custom judges referenced by an ENABLED config are locked against edit and delete
how.note: Deleting a config keeps its results log group. Two ENABLED configs on one agent judge the same sessions twice.
how.insightsNote: INSIGHTS MODE — instead of scoring, sampled sessions are clustered into failure / intent / summary reports on the chosen cadence; a report covers only the sessions the config sampled. Scores and insights cannot share one config — create two on the same agent if you need both.

ab.title: CONFIG-BUNDLE A/B EXPERIMENT
ab.body: Instead of editing and redeploying by hand, let an experiment recommend a new system prompt (and tool descriptions) from the traces, route half of the traffic to each variant through a configuration bundle and settle the verdict with the same evaluators. A managed Harness cannot consume a routed bundle, so the experiment runs on a Runtime twin of this Agent:

The Harness is left untouched, but once the twin is active it becomes the main version of these steps: Chat, evaluation runs and the experiment target it. Note that memory is partitioned per Agent, so the twin starts with an empty long-term memory of its own.

manual.body: The proposal listed these items as manual work — the platform never creates them:

online.title: When the offline scores hold, enable online evaluation
online.body: Online evaluation samples live sessions with the same evaluators — leave the reference-dependent ones off there. Turn it on only once the offline run is stable, and start with a low sampling rate.

assistantNext.note: Guidance only, with two exceptions: START EVALUATION submits a real run (the same request as New Run) and CONVERT TO RUNTIME deploys a new Runtime agent — both after you confirm. Every other link just opens an existing console page with the resources pre-selected — nothing else here invokes the Agent or changes AWS.

recommend.title: Generate AI-recommended improvements
recommend.body: An AI recommendation reads the traces of the run you pick (the newest usable run by default — clean, or one that only lost fewer than half of its sessions to incomplete traces; any of this agent's runs, on any dataset) and proposes a revised system prompt (and tool descriptions): AgentCore Recommendations aimed at the evaluator you pick by default, or GEPA-lite. Review the diff; you can still edit the prompt when accepting, and Launchpad re-publishes the Harness with the final text, so AWS creates a new Harness version (DEFAULT follows it).

recommend.waiting: Available once step 2 has a usable run — its traces seed the recommendation.

blocked.low_coverage: A run completed partially but scored fewer than half of its sessions, so it cannot seed a recommendation. Run again.
blocked.legacy: A run completed partially and predates the failure details. Click “Read failure details” in step 2 — if it only lost traces, the run can seed a recommendation.
blocked.unknown: A run completed partially and AWS gave no reason for the unscored sessions, so it cannot seed a recommendation. Run again.

canary.title: Canary experiment
canary.body: A/B the newest Harness version (the recommendation you accepted) against an earlier version: a dedicated Gateway splits traffic between two Harness endpoints and each variant is scored by its own online evaluation. The 90/10 stage can be dropped at creation to start at 50/50; once the 50/50 verdict is treatment-wins or a tie you can complete right away (1/99 is optional; a tie or a non-significant result needs your explicit confirmation); control-wins rolls back.

These are real, billable AWS resources; while the canary runs, platform invocations of this agent go through the canary Gateway. Clean them up from the canary page when you are done.

mcp.contractBody:
Serve MCP over streamable HTTP at 0.0.0.0:8000/mcp (the AgentCore Runtime MCP contract).

Python (official MCP SDK):
  from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
  mcp = FastMCP(host="0.0.0.0", stateless_http=True)

  @mcp.tool()
  def find_order(order_id: str) -> str:
      """Look up one order."""
      ...

  if __name__ == "__main__":
      mcp.run(transport="streamable-http")

Pin mcp>=1.10,<2 in requirements.txt (mcp 2.x renamed FastMCP to MCPServer). A stdio-only server must be switched to streamable HTTP first.

glossary.agent: An AI assistant you configure once, then chat with or call from other apps.
glossary.harness: A managed agent loop hosted by AgentCore: pick a model, a prompt and tools — no code or container to build.
glossary.runtime: The AgentCore service that runs an agent's code in an isolated, auto-scaling container; the resource name identifies it in AWS.
glossary.registry: A shared catalog where agents, MCP servers and skills are published so others can find and reuse them.
glossary.gateway: One secure entry point that turns APIs and tools into MCP tools your agents can call.
glossary.mcp: Model Context Protocol — an open standard for connecting agents to external tools and data.
glossary.cedarPolicy: A rule in the Cedar language that allows or denies what an agent's tools may do, checked on every call.
glossary.knowledgeBase: A searchable store of your documents that the agent looks things up in, so it answers with your own facts.
glossary.memory: Lets the agent remember the current conversation and, optionally, long-term facts about each user.
glossary.evaluator: A scoring rule, often an LLM judge, that rates agent answers for qualities such as correctness or helpfulness.
glossary.onlineEvaluation: Continuously scores a sample of live conversations so quality drops show up early.
glossary.dataset: A set of test questions, optionally with expected answers, used to evaluate an agent repeatably.
glossary.experiment: An A/B comparison of two agent configurations on the same traffic or data to pick the better one.
glossary.canary: Sends a small share of traffic to a new version first, so it can be rolled back before everyone is affected.
glossary.skill: A reusable package of instructions and files that teaches an agent how to do one specific task.
glossary.a2a: Agent-to-Agent protocol — a standard that lets agents discover and call each other.
glossary.workspace: An isolated environment (one AWS account and region) with its own agents, keys and data.
glossary.observability: Traces, latency, errors and token usage that show how your agents behave in production.
glossary.trace: The step-by-step record of one request: every model call and tool call, with timings.
glossary.criteria: A criterion is the atomic unit of a standard: one checkable statement with a dimension, a tier (red line / gate / observe) and whoever decides it.
